info.title: Evaluating hardware latencies with the hardware latency detector

abstract.para: The hardware latency detector (hwlatdetect) drives the built-in hwlat ftrace tracer of the kernel through tracefs, and identifies system delays introduced directly by platform firmware and hardware, independent of the operating system scheduler.

topic.para: Before you run this test, make sure that the platform firmware is optimized as described in , that the system is running the kernel-rt kernel installed in , and that you are logged in as &rootuser; or can run commands with sudo.

step.para: Start the detector with a specified threshold:
This command monitors system management interrupts (SMIs) with a minimum latency threshold of 10 microseconds.
A run against a tuned, real-time-capable system produces output similar to the following:
step.screen:
&prompt.sudo;hwlatdetect --threshold=10 --duration=120 hwlatdetect: test duration 120 seconds detector: hwlat parameters: Latency threshold: 10us Sample window: 1000000us Sample width: 500000us Non-sampling period: 500000us Output File: None
Starting test test finished Max Latency: 3us Samples recorded: 0 Samples exceeding threshold: 0
step.para: Max Latency reports the largest gap observed between the CPU Time Stamp Counter reads, in microseconds. Samples exceeding threshold counts how many of those gaps were larger than the value you passed with --threshold.

A hardware platform suitable for real-time workloads should report Samples exceeding threshold: 0 over the full test duration, with Max Latency below the threshold you set. If Samples exceeding threshold is greater than zero, or Max Latency approaches or exceeds your threshold, the platform firmware or hardware is introducing delays your application deadline cannot tolerate. Treat this as a hardware or firmware-level failure regardless of what cyclictest reports later, and use a different hardware platform.
